name: Paranasal implants

lead: Paranasal implants are surgical implants placed on the bone beside the nose, in the area between the cheekbone and the upper lip. They add volume where the midface is flat or hollow.
The payoff is a more projected midface and a smoother profile. Studies are mostly case series and cohorts; one study of 33 patients found measurable soft-tissue change over the implant.

paras: A surgeon places a shaped implant, often porous polyethylene or patient-specific material, through an incision, sometimes alongside jaw surgery.
Reported complications include discomfort, sinusitis and tear-duct dysfunction that resolved after plate removal in one series. Forum users also discuss smile changes from over-projection.

angle.text: The implant adds volume exactly where the paranasal area is flat, producing a more projected midface in profile.

lead: Paranasal implants, or paranasal augmentation, add volume to the paranasal area beside the nose where hollowing or flatness is present. They are a hardmaxxing topic on looksmax.org, where posters ask about midface implants and compare them with Le Fort I surgery for sunken midface.[1][2]

In a study of 33 patients, 3 mm porous polyethylene paranasal augmentation combined with mandibular setback was compared with setback alone in 35 patients, with soft-tissue change measured at 6 months.[3]

Surgeons also address paranasal flatness through a modified Le Fort I step osteotomy; a series of 24 patients all achieved a convex cheekbone-nose-lip contour, with 8% having plate discomfort and 8% sinusitis.[4] Patient-specific PMMA implants combined with Le Fort I were reported in two patients with satisfactory results at two years.[5]

paras: Paranasal flatness appears in maxillary deficiency and in conditions such as cleft lip and palate, where skeletal paranasal asymmetry was measured in 30 patients, with the affected side 3.8 mm further back at the piriform aperture.[6]
Forum threads ask how to tell whether one has paranasal flatness and compare implants with Le Fort I.[2][7] Some users warn that too much projection can alter the smile.[2]

Surgical series report plate discomfort, sinusitis and one case of nasolacrimal duct dysfunction.[4] Planning studies assess proximity to the nasolacrimal duct for paranasal implants in the atrophic maxilla.[8]
Studies include a 33-patient porous polyethylene comparison, a 24-case Le Fort step series, and two-patient patient-specific implant reports.[3][4][5] Evidence is mostly small and retrospective.

lore.intro: Hardmaxx forums discuss paranasal implants as a way to fix a sunken midface.[1][2]
